description: Repeated runs of `python3 tools/mochi-soul-engine/engine.py benchmark`, recorded to source the idle figure quoted in README.md (~0.76 us/tick). Each run was a separate process; the per-run metrics are copied unchanged from the report that the engine writes.

machine.cpu: Intel Xeon (virtualised), x86_64, 8 cores, 1 thread per core
machine.scope: Shared Linux VM. The benchmark is single-threaded Python, so one core is busy during a run.

load_note: The VM was not dedicated, so 'idle' means no heavy work was competing for the benchmark core, not a quiet machine. Only the 1-minute load average before each run was recorded (1.07-1.39 on 8 cores); no after-run load, steal time or CPU-time data was captured. The load average does not separate the slow runs from the fast ones: runs 8 and 9 started at 1.18 and 1.08, inside the same band as the other runs, so the cause of their ~1.5 us/tick is not established. Run 5 has a normal tick (0.751 us) but a slow SQLite write (6.52 us) and read (5.94 us); the cause is also not established. No run was dropped. Results are host-CPU numbers, not device speed.
outlier_rule: A run is flagged tick_outlier when its us_per_math_tick is above 1.5x the median of all 12 runs, and sqlite_write_outlier when its us_per_sqlite_write is above 1.5x the median of all 12 runs. The flags are a statistical filter, not a claim about the cause. The rule and its 1.5x threshold were set after the 12 runs had been seen, so they describe this data set; they were not fixed in advance.

us_per_math_tick_without_tick_outliers.note: Sensitivity check only. It is not used for any headline figure.

summary.readme_figure: One method for every headline: the median of all 12 runs, for ticks and for SQLite writes. ~0.76 us/tick = median of all 12 runs (0.7625). ~4.0 us/tx = median of all 12 runs (3.974). Outlier runs (8 and 9 for ticks; 5 and 9 for writes) stay in and are disclosed. The outlier rule was set after the data had been seen.
